style.vernacular: Soviet-planned city at the foot of the snow-capped Trans-Ili Alatau on a grid of tree-lined avenues: 4-9 storey pastel-painted render and panel apartment blocks, brick and concrete institutional buildings, marble-faced Soviet modernist civic landmarks (Wedding Palace, Lenin Palace), Russian-era timber and brick churches, plus post-2000 glass-and-aluminium towers and malls. Flat bitumen or grey/green metal roofs, wide paved boulevards, poplar, elm, spruce and wild-apple trees, and the mountains always on the southern horizon.
style.ornament: Kazakh national ornament (koshkar-muiz ram-horn motif) in sun-grille screens and mosaics on Soviet civic buildings; yurt/shanyrak-inspired circular forms; Soviet mosaic panels and bas-reliefs; Russian Orthodox onion domes on timber and brick churches; white marble and polished granite on landmark facades; glass-and-aluminium cladding on newer stations and malls.

sources.what: Soviet earthquake-resistant housing, schools and cultural venues 1966-72 (Lenin Palace, Hotel Kazakhstan); brick after the 1887 quake; Zenkov Cathedral timber; foothills of Trans-Ili Alatau 700-900 m; humid continental climate
white marble facade with circular glazing, polished granite plinth, Kazakh-ornament sun grilles, yurt-shaped interior (1971)
glass and aluminium cladding on the 1969-75 rebuilt station
